newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian soybean prices firm on poor arrivals.
newsitem.headline: Indian soybean prices firm on poor arrivals.

text.p: Poor soybean arrivals in the Indian markets amid good demand from processing plants drove prices higher, traders said on Friday.
They said the 1996/97 (November-October) soybean crop was expected to be lower than an earlier estimate of 4.0 million tonnes. Arrivals had also fallen as farmers held back stocks.
The soybean crop will be barely 3.6-3.7 million tonnes and farmers are also holding back stocks to sell later at better prices," said one leading oilmeal broker.
"So, prices have reached a record high," he said.
Traders said soymeal was quoted around 11,800-12,400 rupees per tonne compared to around 9,300-9,500 this time last year.

On Wednesday, O.P. Goenka, president of the Central Organisation of Oil Industry and Trade (COOIT) said soybean production in 1996/97 would be a maximum of 3.7 million tonnes compared to 4.2 million in the previous season.
The Soybean Processors Association of India had forecast the 1996/97 crop at 4.0 million tonnes.
Traders said soybean arrivals have trickled down to nearly 3,000 tonnes per day compared to 20,000 tonnes same time last year in the central Indian markets, the hub of India's soybean industry.
They said processing plants were operating at only 30 to 40 percent of capacity against 70 to 80 percent a year ago.
Export demand for Indian soymeal was dull and Indian exporters have signed contracts to export 1.55 million tonnes of soymeal in 1996/97, traders said.
Indian soymeal export prices were quoted at $278-279 per tonne FAS against $275 per tonne last week, traders said. This time last year prices were around $230 per tonne.
